raw: CHAPTER XIII. Fifty-two
en: [Chapter 13] Fifty-two

raw: In the black prison of the Conciergerie, the doomed of the day awaited their fate.
en: In the dark prison of the Conciergerie, the people condemned to die that day waited for their fate.
ko: 콩시에르주리의 어두운 감옥에서, 그날 죽음을 선고받은 사람들이 자신들의 운명을 기다리고 있었다.

raw: They were in number as the weeks of the year.
en: There were fifty-two of them, matching the number of weeks in a year.
ko: 일 년의 주(週) 수와 같은 쉰두 명이었다.

raw: Fifty-two were to roll that afternoon on the life-tide of the city to the boundless everlasting sea.
en: That afternoon, fifty-two lives would be carried away on the city's tide of death to the endless ocean of eternity.
ko: 그날 오후, 쉰두 개의 목숨이 죽음이라는 도시의 조류에 휩쓸려 영원의 끝없는 바다로 떠내려갈 것이었다.

raw: Before their cells were quit of them, new occupants were appointed; before their blood ran into the blood spilled yesterday, the blood that was to mingle with theirs to-morrow was already set apart.
en: Before they even left their cells, new prisoners were assigned to replace them. Before their blood could join the blood spilled yesterday, the blood of those to be executed tomorrow was already being chosen.
ko: 그들이 감방을 떠나기도 전에, 그들을 대신할 새로운 죄수들이 배정되었다. 그들의 피가 어제 흘린 피와 섞이기도 전에, 내일 처형될 사람들의 피가 이미 선택되고 있었다.

raw: Two score and twelve were told off.
en: Exactly fifty-two people were counted off.
ko: 정확히 쉰두 명의 사람들이 세어졌다.

raw: From the farmer-general of seventy, whose riches could not buy his life, to the seamstress of twenty, whose poverty and obscurity could not save her.
en: They ranged from a seventy-year-old wealthy tax collector, whose money could not buy his freedom, to a twenty-year-old seamstress, whose poverty and simple life could not save her.
ko: 자신의 돈으로 자유를 살 수 없었던 70세의 부유한 세금 징수원부터, 가난과 소박한 삶으로도 자신을 구할 수 없었던 20세의 재봉사까지 다양했다.

raw: Physical diseases, engendered in the vices and neglects of men, will seize on victims of all degrees; and the frightful moral disorder, born of unspeakable suffering, intolerable oppression, and heartless indifference, smote equally without distinction.
en: Just as physical diseases, born of human vice and neglect, strike down people of all classes, this terrifying moral sickness, born of unspeakable suffering, unbearable oppression, and cruel indifference, struck everyone down without distinction.
ko: 인간의 악덕과 방치에서 비롯된 육체적 질병이 모든 계층의 사람들을 쓰러뜨리듯이, 말할 수 없는 고통과 견딜 수 없는 억압, 잔인한 무관심에서 태어난 이 끔찍한 도덕적 질병은 차별 없이 모든 사람을 쓰러뜨렸다.

raw: Charles Darnay, alone in a cell, had sustained himself with no flattering delusion since he came to it from the Tribunal.
en: Charles Darnay, alone in a cell, had not fooled himself with any false hopes since returning from the courtroom.
ko: 감방에 홀로 남은 찰스 다네이는 법정에서 돌아온 이후 어떠한 헛된 희망으로도 자신을 속이지 않았다.

raw: In every line of the narrative he had heard, he had heard his condemnation.
en: In every line of the story he had heard read, he heard his death sentence.
ko: 그가 들었던 이야기의 모든 구절에서 그는 자신의 사형 선고를 들었다.

raw: He had fully comprehended that no personal influence could possibly save him, that he was virtually sentenced by the millions, and that units could avail him nothing.
en: He fully understood that no personal influence could save him now, that he was essentially condemned by millions of people, and that a few individuals could do nothing to help him.
ko: 그는 이제 어떠한 개인적 영향력으로도 자신을 구할 수 없으며, 자신이 본질적으로 수백만 명의 사람들에게 정죄받았고, 소수의 사람들은 자신을 돕기 위해 아무것도 할 수 없다는 것을 완전히 이해했다.

raw: Nevertheless, it was not easy, with the face of his beloved wife fresh before him, to compose his mind to what it must bear.
en: Still, with the face of his beloved wife fresh in his memory, it was not easy to prepare his mind for what was coming.
ko: 그럼에도 불구하고, 사랑하는 아내의 얼굴이 기억 속에 생생하게 남아 있었기에, 다가올 일을 위해 마음의 준비를 하는 것은 쉽지 않았다.

raw: His hold on life was strong, and it was very, very hard, to loosen; by gradual efforts and degrees unclosed a little here, it clenched the tighter there; and when he brought his strength to bear on that hand and it yielded, this was closed again.
en: His grip on life was strong, and it was very, very hard to let go. As he slowly pried one finger loose, another gripped even tighter; and when he forced his hand to open, it clamped shut again.
ko: 그의 삶에 대한 집착은 강렬했고, 그것을 놓아버리기는 너무나도 힘들었다. 그가 천천히 손가락 하나를 떼어내면, 다른 손가락이 더욱 꽉 쥐어졌고, 억지로 손을 펴면, 다시 꽉 닫혀버렸다.

raw: There was a hurry, too, in all his thoughts, a turbulent and heated working of his heart, that contended against resignation.
en: His thoughts were racing, and his heart pounded with a wild energy that fought against giving up.
ko: 그의 생각은 빠르게 내달렸고, 심장은 포기하지 않으려고 발버둥 치는 거친 에너지로 요동쳤다.

raw: If, for a moment, he did feel resigned, then his wife and child who had to live after him, seemed to protest and to make it a selfish thing.
en: If he felt at peace with his fate for even a second, the thought of his wife and child living on without him made his peace feel selfish.
ko: 그가 단 1초라도 자신의 운명에 평온함을 느낀다면, 자신 없이 살아갈 아내와 아이에 대한 생각이 그 평온함을 이기적인 것으로 느끼게 만들었다.

raw: But, all this was at first.
en: But that was only at first.
ko: 하지만 그것은 처음에만 그랬다.

raw: Before long, the consideration that there was no disgrace in the fate he must meet, and that numbers went the same road wrongfully, and trod it firmly every day, sprang up to stimulate him.
en: Before long, the thought that there was no shame in the death he faced, and that many others went to the same death unjustly and stood strong every day, helped encourage him.
ko: 머지않아, 자신이 직면한 죽음에 부끄러움이 없으며, 다른 많은 이들도 매일 부당하게 같은 죽음을 맞이하면서도 굳건히 서 있다는 생각이 그에게 용기를 주었다.

raw: Next followed the thought that much of the future peace of mind enjoyable by the dear ones, depended on his quiet fortitude.
en: Next came the thought that much of his family's future peace of mind depended on his quiet courage.
ko: 다음으로는 가족의 미래의 마음의 평화가 자신의 조용한 용기에 크게 달려 있다는 생각이 들었다.

raw: So, by degrees he calmed into the better state, when he could raise his thoughts much higher, and draw comfort down.
en: So, step by step, he calmed down, lifting his thoughts to higher things and finding comfort.
ko: 그래서 그는 한 걸음씩 차분해졌고, 자신의 생각을 더 높은 곳으로 끌어올리며 위안을 찾았다.

raw: Before it had set in dark on the night of his condemnation, he had travelled thus far on his last way.
en: Before darkness fell on the night of his sentencing, he had traveled this far along his path to death.
ko: 선고를 받은 날 밤의 어둠이 내리기 전에, 그는 죽음을 향한 길을 이만큼이나 걸어왔다.

raw: Being allowed to purchase the means of writing, and a light, he sat down to write until such time as the prison lamps should be extinguished.
en: Being allowed to buy writing materials and a candle, he sat down to write until the prison lights were put out.
ko: 필기도구와 양초를 사는 것이 허락되어, 그는 감옥의 불이 꺼질 때까지 앉아서 글을 썼다.

raw: He wrote a long letter to Lucie, showing her that he had known nothing of her father’s imprisonment, until he had heard of it from herself, and that he had been as ignorant as she of his father’s and uncle’s responsibility for that misery, until the paper had been read.
en: He wrote a long letter to Lucie, explaining that he had known nothing about her father's time in prison until she told him about it. He had been just as ignorant as she was about his father's and uncle's responsibility for that suffering until the paper was read in court.
ko: 그는 루시에게 긴 편지를 써서, 그녀가 말해주기 전까지는 그녀 아버지의 수감 생활에 대해 전혀 몰랐다고 설명했다. 법정에서 그 문건이 낭독될 때까지 그도 그 고통에 대한 자신의 아버지와 삼촌의 책임에 대해 그녀만큼이나 무지했다.

raw: He had already explained to her that his concealment from herself of the name he had relinquished, was the one condition--fully intelligible now--that her father had attached to their betrothal, and was the one promise he had still exacted on the morning of their marriage.
en: He reminded her that hiding his real family name from her was the one condition, which made complete sense now, that her father had placed on their engagement, and the one promise he had kept on their wedding morning.
ko: 그는 자신의 진짜 가문 이름을 그녀에게 숨기는 것이 이제야 완전히 이해가 되는, 아버지가 그들의 약혼에 내건 유일한 조건이었으며, 결혼식 날 아침 그가 지킨 유일한 약속이었음을 그녀에게 상기시켰다.

raw: He entreated her, for her father’s sake, never to seek to know whether her father had become oblivious of the existence of the paper, or had had it recalled to him (for the moment, or for good), by the story of the Tower, on that old Sunday under the dear old plane-tree in the garden.
en: He begged her, for her father's sake, never to try to find out if her father had forgotten about the paper or had been reminded of it by the story of the Tower on that old Sunday under the plane tree in the garden.
ko: 그는 아버지를 위해서라도, 아버지가 그 문건을 잊었었는지 아니면 정원의 플라타너스 아래에서 보냈던 예전의 어느 일요일에 런던 탑 이야기에 의해 그것을 떠올렸던 것인지 알아내려 하지 말아달라고 그녀에게 간청했다.

raw: If he had preserved any definite remembrance of it, there could be no doubt that he had supposed it destroyed with the Bastille, when he had found no mention of it among the relics of prisoners which the populace had discovered there, and which had been described to all the world.
en: Darnay wrote that if Doctor Manette had remembered it at all, he surely thought it was destroyed when the Bastille fell, since it wasn't mentioned among the records found there.
ko: 다네이는 마네트 박사가 그것을 조금이라도 기억했다면, 그곳에서 발견된 기록들 중에 그것이 언급되지 않았기 때문에 바스티유가 함락될 때 그것이 파괴되었다고 확신했을 것이라고 썼다.

raw: He besought her--though he added that he knew it was needless--to console her father, by impressing him through every tender means she could think of, with the truth that he had done nothing for which he could justly reproach himself, but had uniformly forgotten himself for their joint sakes.
en: He begged her, though he knew he didn't need to ask, to comfort her father by gently showing him that he had done nothing to blame himself for, but had always put himself last for their sakes.
ko: 그는 굳이 부탁할 필요가 없다는 것을 알면서도, 아버지가 스스로를 자책할 일이 아무것도 없으며 항상 그들을 위해 자신을 맨 뒷전에 두었음을 다정하게 보여주어 그를 위로해 달라고 그녀에게 간청했다.

raw: Next to her preservation of his own last grateful love and blessing, and her overcoming of her sorrow, to devote herself to their dear child, he adjured her, as they would meet in Heaven, to comfort her father.
en: After asking her to hold onto his grateful love and blessing, and to overcome her grief to focus on their dear child, he begged her, by their hope of meeting in Heaven, to comfort her father.
ko: 자신의 감사하는 사랑과 축복을 간직하고 슬픔을 이겨내어 그들의 소중한 아이에게 집중해 달라고 부탁한 후, 그는 천국에서 만날 희망을 걸고 아버지를 위로해 줄 것을 그녀에게 간청했다.

raw: To her father himself, he wrote in the same strain; but, he told her father that he expressly confided his wife and child to his care.
en: To her father, he wrote in the same way, but he explicitly left his wife and child in the Doctor's care.
ko: 그는 그녀의 아버지에게도 같은 방식으로 썼지만, 자신의 아내와 아이를 박사의 보살핌에 명시적으로 맡겼다.

raw: And he told him this, very strongly, with the hope of rousing him from any despondency or dangerous retrospect towards which he foresaw he might be tending.
en: He wrote this very strongly, hoping to keep the Doctor from falling into despair or dwelling on the dangerous past, which Darnay feared might happen.
ko: 그는 다네이가 우려했던 대로 박사가 절망에 빠지거나 위험한 과거에 연연하는 것을 막기를 바라며 이 부분을 매우 강하게 썼다.

raw: To Mr.
en: To Mr.
ko: 로리 씨에게,

raw: Lorry, he commended them all, and explained his worldly affairs.
en: Lorry, he entrusted the family and explained his financial affairs.
ko: 그는 가족을 부탁하며 자신의 재정 문제를 설명했다.

raw: That done, with many added sentences of grateful friendship and warm attachment, all was done.
en: Once that was done, along with many words of grateful friendship and love, his task was complete.
ko: 그 일이 끝나자, 감사하는 우정과 사랑의 많은 말들과 함께 그의 임무는 완료되었다.

raw: He never thought of Carton.
en: He never thought of Carton.
ko: 그는 카턴에 대해서는 전혀 생각하지 않았다.

raw: His mind was so full of the others, that he never once thought of him.
en: His mind was so full of his family that he did not think of him once.
ko: 그의 마음은 가족으로 너무 가득 차 있어서 그를 단 한 번도 생각하지 않았다.

raw: He had time to finish these letters before the lights were put out.
en: He had time to finish these letters before the lights were turned off.
ko: 그는 불이 꺼지기 전에 이 편지들을 마칠 시간이 있었다.

raw: When he lay down on his straw bed, he thought he had done with this world.
en: When he lay down on his straw bed, he believed he was done with this world for good.
ko: 지푸라기 침대에 누웠을 때, 그는 이 세상과의 인연이 영원히 끝났다고 믿었다.

raw: But, it beckoned him back in his sleep, and showed itself in shining forms.
en: But the world pulled him back in his sleep, showing itself in beautiful dreams.
ko: 하지만 세상은 그의 꿈속에 아름다운 모습으로 나타나 그를 잠결에 다시 끌어당겼다.

raw: Free and happy, back in the old house in Soho (though it had nothing in it like the real house), unaccountably released and light of heart, he was with Lucie again, and she told him it was all a dream, and he had never gone away.
en: Free and happy, back in the old house in Soho, though the dream house looked nothing like the real one, mysteriously released and lighthearted, he was with Lucie again. She told him it was all a dream and that he had never left.
ko: 자유롭고 행복하게, 비록 꿈속의 집은 실제와는 전혀 다르게 생겼지만 소호의 옛집으로 돌아가서, 신비롭게 풀려나 가벼운 마음으로 그는 다시 루시와 함께 있었다. 그녀는 그에게 이 모든 것이 꿈이며 그가 결코 떠난 적이 없다고 말했다.

raw: A pause of forgetfulness, and then he had even suffered, and had come back to her, dead and at peace, and yet there was no difference in him.
en: After a moment of blankness, he dreamed he had suffered and come back to her, dead and at peace, yet looking exactly the same.
ko: 잠깐의 멍한 순간이 지난 후, 그는 고통을 겪고 죽어 평화로운 상태로, 하지만 예전과 똑같은 모습으로 그녀에게 돌아가는 꿈을 꾸었다.

raw: Another pause of oblivion, and he awoke in the sombre morning, unconscious where he was or what had happened, until it flashed upon his mind, “this is the day of my death!”
en: Another moment of sleep, and then he woke up in the gloomy morning, not knowing where he was or what had happened, until it flashed in his mind: “This is the day of my death!”
ko: 또 한순간 잠이 들었다가 어두침침한 아침에 깨어난 그는 자신이 어디에 있는지, 무슨 일이 일어났는지 알지 못하다가, 머릿속에 번뜩이는 생각이 스쳤다. “오늘이 내 죽음의 날이구나!”

raw: Thus, had he come through the hours, to the day when the fifty-two heads were to fall.
en: So he had lived through the hours to the day when the fifty-two heads were to fall.
ko: 그렇게 그는 쉰두 개의 머리가 떨어질 날까지 시간들을 견뎌내며 살아남았던 것이다.

raw: And now, while he was composed, and hoped that he could meet the end with quiet heroism, a new action began in his waking thoughts, which was very difficult to master.
en: Now, though he was calm and hoped to face the end with quiet courage, a new train of thought began in his mind that was very hard to control.
ko: 이제 그는 차분했고 조용한 용기로 마지막을 맞이하기를 바랐지만, 통제하기 매우 어려운 새로운 생각들이 그의 마음속에서 시작되었다.

raw: He had never seen the instrument that was to terminate his life.
en: He had never seen the Guillotine that was to end his life. How high was it from the ground? How many steps did it have?
ko: 그는 자신의 목숨을 끝낼 단두대를 본 적이 없었다. 그것은 땅에서 얼마나 높이 떨어져 있을까? 계단은 몇 개나 될까?

raw: How high it was from the ground, how many steps it had, where he would be stood, how he would be touched, whether the touching hands would be dyed red, which way his face would be turned, whether he would be the first, or might be the last: these and many similar questions, in nowise directed by his will, obtruded themselves over and over again, countless times.
en: Where would he stand? How would they touch him, and would the hands that touched him be stained red? Which way would his face be turned? Would he be the first to die, or the last? These and many similar questions, which he did not want to think about, forced themselves into his mind over and over again.
ko: 그는 어디에 서게 될까? 그들이 그를 어떻게 만질 것이며, 그를 만지는 손은 붉게 물들어 있을까? 그의 얼굴은 어느 쪽을 향하게 될까? 그가 첫 번째로 죽게 될까, 아니면 마지막일까? 그가 생각하고 싶지 않은 이러한 것들과 이와 비슷한 많은 질문들이 계속해서 그의 마음속으로 밀려들었다.

raw: Neither were they connected with fear: he was conscious of no fear.
en: It was not out of fear; he felt no fear.
ko: 그것은 두려움 때문이 아니었다. 그는 두려움을 느끼지 않았다.

raw: Rather, they originated in a strange besetting desire to know what to do when the time came; a desire gigantically disproportionate to the few swift moments to which it referred; a wondering that was more like the wondering of some other spirit within his, than his own.
en: Rather, it came from a strange, nagging desire to know what to do when the moment arrived, a desire far larger than the few quick seconds it concerned. It was a curiosity that felt more like it belonged to some other spirit inside him than to himself.
ko: 오히려 그것은 그 순간이 왔을 때 무엇을 해야 할지 알고 싶어 하는 이상하고도 괴롭히는 욕망, 즉 관련된 짧은 몇 초보다 훨씬 더 큰 욕망에서 비롯되었다. 그것은 그 자신보다는 그의 내면에 있는 다른 어떤 영혼에 속한 것처럼 느껴지는 호기심이었다.

raw: The hours went on as he walked to and fro, and the clocks struck the numbers he would never hear again.
en: The hours passed as he walked back and forth, and the clocks struck the hours he would never hear again.
ko: 그가 이리저리 걷는 동안 시간은 흘렀고, 시계는 그가 다시는 듣지 못할 시간들을 울렸다.

raw: Nine gone for ever, ten gone for ever, eleven gone for ever, twelve coming on to pass away.
en: Nine o'clock gone forever, ten o'clock gone forever, eleven o'clock gone forever, and twelve o'clock coming and going.
ko: 9시가 영원히 지나갔고, 10시가 영원히 지나갔으며, 11시도 영원히 지나갔고, 12시가 다가왔다 지나갔다.

raw: After a hard contest with that eccentric action of thought which had last perplexed him, he had got the better of it.
en: After a hard struggle with the strange thoughts that had bothered him, he finally overcame them.
ko: 그를 괴롭히던 이상한 생각들과 힘든 싸움을 벌인 후, 그는 마침내 그것들을 이겨냈다.

raw: He walked up and down, softly repeating their names to himself.
en: He walked up and down, softly repeating the names of his loved ones to himself.
ko: 그는 사랑하는 이들의 이름을 혼자 부드럽게 반복하며 위아래로 걸었다.

raw: The worst of the strife was over.
en: The worst of the struggle was over.
ko: 가장 힘든 싸움은 끝났다.

raw: He could walk up and down, free from distracting fancies, praying for himself and for them.
en: He could walk back and forth, free from distracting thoughts, praying for himself and for them.
ko: 그는 산만한 생각들에서 벗어나, 자신과 그들을 위해 기도하며 이리저리 걸을 수 있었다.

raw: Twelve gone for ever.
en: Twelve o'clock gone forever.
ko: 12시가 영원히 지나갔다.

raw: He had been apprised that the final hour was Three, and he knew he would be summoned some time earlier, inasmuch as the tumbrils jolted heavily and slowly through the streets.
en: He had been told that the execution was at three o'clock, and he knew he would be called earlier, since the death carts traveled heavily and slowly through the streets.
ko: 그는 처형이 3시라고 들었고, 죽음의 수레가 거리를 무겁고 느리게 이동하기 때문에 더 일찍 불릴 것이라는 것을 알았다.

raw: Therefore, he resolved to keep Two before his mind, as the hour, and so to strengthen himself in the interval that he might be able, after that time, to strengthen others.
en: Therefore, he decided to focus on two o'clock as the final hour, using the time before then to build up his strength so he could help others when the time came.
ko: 그래서 그는 2시를 마지막 시간으로 정하고, 그때까지 체력을 길러 때가 되면 다른 사람들을 도울 수 있도록 하기로 결정했다.

raw: Walking regularly to and fro with his arms folded on his breast, a very different man from the prisoner, who had walked to and fro at La Force, he heard One struck away from him, without surprise.
en: Walking steadily back and forth with his arms crossed over his chest, looking very different from the panicked prisoner who had paced in La Force prison, he heard the clock strike one without surprise.
ko: 팔을 가슴에 교차시킨 채 이리저리 꾸준히 걸으며, 라 포스 감옥에서 서성거리던 겁먹은 죄수와는 전혀 다른 모습으로, 그는 1시를 알리는 시계 소리를 놀라움 없이 들었다.

raw: The hour had measured like most other hours.
en: The hour had felt like any other hour.
ko: 그 한 시간은 여느 때와 다름없이 느껴졌다.

raw: Devoutly thankful to Heaven for his recovered self-possession, he thought, “There is but another now,” and turned to walk again.
en: Deeply thankful to Heaven for regaining his self-control, he thought, “There is only one hour left now,” and turned to walk again.
ko: 자제력을 되찾은 것에 대해 하늘에 깊이 감사하며, 그는 “이제 한 시간밖에 남지 않았어,”라고 생각하고 다시 걷기 위해 돌아섰다.

raw: Footsteps in the stone passage outside the door.
en: Footsteps in the stone hallway outside the door.
ko: 문 밖 돌 복도에서 발소리가 들렸다.

raw: He stopped.
en: He stopped.
ko: 그는 멈춰 섰다.

raw: The key was put in the lock, and turned.
en: A key was put in the lock and turned.
ko: 자물쇠에 열쇠가 꽂히고 돌아갔다.

raw: Before the door was opened, or as it opened, a man said in a low voice, in English: “He has never seen me here; I have kept out of his way.
en: Before the door opened, a man said in a quiet English voice: “He has never seen me here; I have stayed out of his sight.
ko: 문이 열리기 전에, 한 남자가 조용한 영어 억양으로 말했다. “그는 여기서 나를 본 적이 없소; 나는 그의 눈에 띄지 않게 숨어 있었소.

raw: Go you in alone; I wait near.
en: Go in alone; I'll wait nearby.
ko: 혼자 들어가시오; 나는 근처에서 기다리겠소.

raw: Lose no time!”
en: Hurry!”
ko: 서두르시오!”

raw: The door was quickly opened and closed, and there stood before him face to face, quiet, intent upon him, with the light of a smile on his features, and a cautionary finger on his lip, Sydney Carton.
en: The door was quickly opened and closed, and there standing face-to-face with him, quiet and focused, with a gentle smile and a warning finger on his lips, was Sydney Carton.
ko: 문이 재빨리 열렸다 닫혔고, 그와 얼굴을 맞대고 서 있는 사람은 조용하고 집중한 채, 부드러운 미소를 지으며 입술에 경고의 손가락을 대고 있는 시드니 카턴이었다.

raw: There was something so bright and remarkable in his look, that, for the first moment, the prisoner misdoubted him to be an apparition of his own imagining.
en: There was something so bright and unusual in Carton's look that, at first, Darnay thought he was just a ghost created by his own imagination.
ko: 카턴의 표정에는 너무나 밝고 특이한 무언가가 있어서, 처음에 다네이는 그가 단지 자신의 상상이 만들어낸 유령일 뿐이라고 생각했다.

raw: But, he spoke, and it was his voice; he took the prisoner’s hand, and it was his real grasp.
en: But Carton spoke, and it was truly his voice; he took Darnay's hand, and it was a real, solid grip.
ko: 하지만 카턴이 말했고, 그것은 진정 그의 목소리였다. 그가 다네이의 손을 잡았고, 그것은 진짜 굳센 악수였다.

raw: “Of all the people upon earth, you least expected to see me?” he said.
en: “Of all the people on earth, I'm the last one you expected to see?” he said.
ko: “이 세상 모든 사람 중에서, 내가 당신이 가장 예상치 못한 사람이겠지요?” 그가 말했다.

raw: “I could not believe it to be you.
en: “I couldn't believe it was you.
ko: “당신일 줄은 믿을 수 없었소.

raw: I can scarcely believe it now.
en: I can barely believe it now.
ko: 지금도 거의 믿기지 않소.

raw: You are not”--the apprehension came suddenly into his mind--“a prisoner?”
en: You aren't”, a sudden fear struck him, “a prisoner?”
ko: 당신은”, 갑작스러운 두려움이 그를 덮쳤다, “죄수가 아니오?”

raw: “No.
en: “No.
ko: “아니오.

raw: I am accidentally possessed of a power over one of the keepers here, and in virtue of it I stand before you.
en: By chance, I have leverage over one of the guards here, and that is why I am standing in front of you.
ko: 우연히, 나는 이곳 경비병 중 한 명에게 영향력을 가지게 되었고, 그래서 당신 앞에 서 있는 것이오.

raw: I come from her--your wife, dear Darnay.”
en: I come from her, your wife, dear Darnay.”
ko: 나는 그녀, 당신의 아내에게서 왔소, 친애하는 다네이.”

raw: The prisoner wrung his hand.
en: Darnay squeezed his hand.
ko: 다네이는 그의 손을 꽉 쥐었다.

raw: “I bring you a request from her.”
en: “I bring you a request from her.”
ko: “그녀의 부탁을 전하러 왔소.”

raw: “What is it?”
en: “What is it?”
ko: “무엇이오?”

raw: “A most earnest, pressing, and emphatic entreaty, addressed to you in the most pathetic tones of the voice so dear to you, that you well remember.”
en: “A very earnest, urgent, and important plea, spoken in the saddest tones of the voice you love so much and remember so well.”
ko: “당신이 그토록 사랑하고 잘 기억하는 목소리의 가장 슬픈 어조로 말한, 매우 간절하고 시급하며 중요한 간청이오.”

raw: The prisoner turned his face partly aside.
en: Darnay turned his face away slightly.
ko: 다네이는 약간 고개를 돌렸다.

raw: “You have no time to ask me why I bring it, or what it means; I have no time to tell you.
en: “You don't have time to ask why I bring this request or what it means, and I don't have time to tell you.
ko: “당신은 내가 왜 이 부탁을 가져왔는지, 혹은 그것이 무슨 의미인지 물을 시간이 없고, 나 역시 당신에게 말해줄 시간이 없소.

raw: You must comply with it--take off those boots you wear, and draw on these of mine.”
en: You must obey, take off your boots and put on mine.”
ko: 당신은 따라야 하오. 부츠를 벗고 내 것을 신으시오.”

raw: There was a chair against the wall of the cell, behind the prisoner.
en: There was a chair against the cell wall behind the prisoner.
ko: 죄수 뒤의 감방 벽에는 의자가 하나 있었다.

raw: Carton, pressing forward, had already, with the speed of lightning, got him down into it, and stood over him, barefoot.
en: Carton pushed forward and, with lightning speed, forced Darnay down into the chair and stood over him, barefoot.
ko: 카턴은 앞으로 밀고 나가 번개 같은 속도로 다네이를 의자에 강제로 앉히고는, 맨발로 그의 위를 굽어보며 섰다.

raw: “Draw on these boots of mine.
en: “Put on my boots.
ko: “내 부츠를 신으시오.

raw: Put your hands to them; put your will to them.
en: Reach down and pull them on; focus your mind.
ko: 허리를 굽혀 끌어올리시오; 정신을 집중하시오.

raw: Quick!”
en: Quick!”
ko: 빨리!”

raw: “Carton, there is no escaping from this place; it never can be done.
en: “Carton, there is no escaping from this place; it's impossible.
ko: “카턴, 이곳에서 탈출하는 것은 불가능하오; 말도 안 되오.

raw: You will only die with me.
en: You will only die with me.
ko: 당신은 단지 나와 함께 죽게 될 뿐이오.

raw: It is madness.”
en: It is madness.”
ko: 이건 미친 짓이오.”

raw: “It would be madness if I asked you to escape; but do I?
en: “It would be madness if I asked you to escape, but did I?
ko: “내가 당신에게 탈출하라고 요구했다면 미친 짓이겠지만, 내가 그랬소?

raw: When I ask you to pass out at that door, tell me it is madness and remain here.
en: When I actually ask you to walk out that door, then you can call me crazy and stay here.
ko: 내가 실제로 저 문 밖으로 걸어 나가라고 요구할 때, 그때 나를 미쳤다고 부르고 여기에 남으시오.

raw: Change that cravat for this of mine, that coat for this of mine.
en: Change your tie for mine, and your coat for mine.
ko: 당신의 넥타이를 내 것과 바꾸고, 코트를 내 것과 바꾸시오.

raw: While you do it, let me take this ribbon from your hair, and shake out your hair like this of mine!”
en: While you do that, let me take the ribbon from your hair and shake it out so it looks like mine!”
ko: 당신이 그렇게 하는 동안, 당신의 머리에서 리본을 풀어내 내 것처럼 보이게 흩뜨려 놓겠소!”

raw: With wonderful quickness, and with a strength both of will and action, that appeared quite supernatural, he forced all these changes upon him.
en: With incredible speed and a strength of will and action that seemed almost superhuman, Carton forced all these changes on him.
ko: 믿을 수 없는 속도와 거의 초인적인 의지와 행동의 힘으로 카턴은 이 모든 변화를 그에게 강요했다.

raw: The prisoner was like a young child in his hands.
en: Darnay was like a little child in his hands.
ko: 다네이는 그의 손안에서 어린아이와 같았다.

raw: “Carton!
en: “Carton!
ko: “카턴!

raw: Dear Carton!
en: Dear Carton!
ko: 친애하는 카턴!

raw: It is madness.
en: This is madness.
ko: 이건 미친 짓이오.

raw: It cannot be accomplished, it never can be done, it has been attempted, and has always failed.
en: It can't be done; it has been tried before and always fails.
ko: 할 수 없소; 예전에도 시도되었지만 항상 실패했소.

raw: I implore you not to add your death to the bitterness of mine.”
en: I beg you not to add your death to the bitterness of my own.”
ko: 저의 죽음의 고통에 당신의 죽음까지 더하지 말아 주시기를 간청합니다.”

raw: “Do I ask you, my dear Darnay, to pass the door?
en: “Am I asking you to walk out the door, my dear Darnay?
ko: “친애하는 다네이, 제가 당신에게 문 밖으로 걸어 나가라고 요구하고 있습니까?

raw: When I ask that, refuse.
en: When I ask that, you can say no.
ko: 제가 그렇게 요구할 때 거절하셔도 됩니다.

raw: There are pen and ink and paper on this table.
en: There is a pen, ink, and paper on this table.
ko: 이 탁자 위에 펜과 잉크, 종이가 있습니다.

raw: Is your hand steady enough to write?”
en: Is your hand steady enough to write?”
ko: 글씨를 쓸 수 있을 만큼 손이 안정되어 있습니까?”

raw: “It was when you came in.”
en: “It was before you came in.”
ko: “당신이 들어오기 전에는 그랬소.”

raw: “Steady it again, and write what I shall dictate.
en: “Steady it again, and write what I tell you.
ko: “다시 손을 진정시키고, 제가 불러주는 대로 적으십시오.

raw: Quick, friend, quick!”
en: Quick, friend, quick!”
ko: 서두르십시오, 친구여, 서두르십시오!”

raw: Pressing his hand to his bewildered head, Darnay sat down at the table.
en: Holding his confused head in his hand, Darnay sat at the table.
ko: 혼란스러운 머리를 감싸 쥐고, 다네이는 탁자에 앉았다.

raw: Carton, with his right hand in his breast, stood close beside him.
en: Carton stood close beside him with his right hand hidden inside his coat.
ko: 카턴은 오른손을 코트 안에 숨긴 채 그의 곁에 바짝 서 있었다.

raw: “Write exactly as I speak.”
en: “Write exactly what I say.”
ko: “제가 말하는 대로 정확히 적으십시오.”

raw: “To whom do I address it?”
en: “Who is this to?”
ko: “누구에게 쓰는 거요?”

raw: “To no one.” Carton still had his hand in his breast.
en: “To no one.” Carton still kept his hand inside his coat.
ko: “아무에게도 쓰는 것이 아닙니다.” 카턴은 여전히 코트 안에 손을 넣고 있었다.

raw: “Do I date it?”
en: “Should I date it?”
ko: “날짜를 적어야 하오?”

raw: “No.”
en: “No.”
ko: “아니요.”

raw: The prisoner looked up, at each question.
en: Darnay looked up at each question.
ko: 다네이는 질문을 할 때마다 고개를 들어 올려다보았다.

raw: Carton, standing over him with his hand in his breast, looked down.
en: Carton stood over him, looking down, with his hand still inside his coat.
ko: 카턴은 여전히 코트 안에 손을 넣은 채로 그를 굽어보고 서 있었다.

raw: “‘If you remember,’” said Carton, dictating, “‘the words that passed between us, long ago, you will readily comprehend this when you see it.
en: “‘If you remember,’” Carton dictated, “‘the words we spoke to each other long ago, you will understand this when you see it.
ko: “‘당신이 기억하신다면,’” 카턴이 구술했다, “‘우리가 오래전에 서로 나누었던 말들을, 당신은 이것을 볼 때 이해하실 것입니다.

raw: You do remember them, I know.
en: I know you remember them.
ko: 당신이 그 말들을 기억하고 있다는 것을 압니다.

raw: It is not in your nature to forget them.’”
en: It is not in your nature to forget them.’”
ko: 그것들을 잊는 것은 당신의 본성이 아니니까요.’”

raw: He was drawing his hand from his breast; the prisoner chancing to look up in his hurried wonder as he wrote, the hand stopped, closing upon something.
en: Carton was drawing his hand out of his coat. When Darnay happened to look up in surprise as he wrote, Carton's hand stopped, holding onto something.
ko: 카턴은 코트에서 손을 빼내고 있었다. 다네이가 글을 쓰다가 놀라서 무심코 고개를 들었을 때, 무언가를 움켜쥐고 있던 카턴의 손이 멈칫했다.

raw: “Have you written ‘forget them’?” Carton asked.
en: “Have you written ‘forget them’?” Carton asked.
ko: “‘그것들을 잊는 것은’까지 적으셨습니까?” 카턴이 물었다.

raw: “I have.
en: “I have.
ko: “적었소.

raw: Is that a weapon in your hand?”
en: Is that a weapon in your hand?”
ko: 당신 손에 있는 것은 무기요?”

raw: “No; I am not armed.”
en: “No, I am not armed.”
ko: “아닙니다, 저는 무기를 들고 있지 않습니다.”

raw: “What is it in your hand?”
en: “What is in your hand?”
ko: “손에 든 것은 무엇이오?”

raw: “You shall know directly.
en: “You will find out in a moment.
ko: “잠시 후에 알게 될 것입니다.

raw: Write on; there are but a few words more.” He dictated again. “‘I am thankful that the time has come, when I can prove them.
en: Keep writing; there are only a few words left.” He dictated again. “‘I am thankful that the time has come when I can prove those words.
ko: 계속 적으십시오; 이제 몇 단어 남지 않았습니다.” 그가 다시 구술했다. “‘제가 그 말들을 증명할 수 있는 때가 왔다는 것에 감사합니다.

raw: That I do so is no subject for regret or grief.’” As he said these words with his eyes fixed on the writer, his hand slowly and softly moved down close to the writer’s face.
en: That I am doing this is no reason for regret or sadness.’” As Carton spoke, keeping his eyes fixed on Darnay, his hand slowly and gently drifted down close to Darnay's face.
ko: 제가 이 일을 하고 있다는 사실이 후회나 슬픔의 이유가 될 수는 없습니다.’” 카턴은 말을 하면서, 다네이에게 시선을 고정한 채, 그의 손을 다네이의 얼굴 가까이로 천천히 부드럽게 내렸다.

raw: The pen dropped from Darnay’s fingers on the table, and he looked about him vacantly.
en: The pen slipped from Darnay's fingers onto the table, and he looked around blankly.
ko: 펜이 다네이의 손가락에서 미끄러져 탁자 위로 떨어졌고, 그는 멍하니 주변을 둘러보았다.

raw: “What vapour is that?” he asked.
en: “What is that smell?” he asked.
ko: “이게 무슨 냄새지?” 그가 물었다.

raw: “Vapour?”
en: “Smell?”
ko: “냄새라뇨?”

raw: “Something that crossed me?”
en: “Something that just passed by me?”
ko: “방금 내 곁을 스쳐간 무언가 말이오?”

raw: “I am conscious of nothing; there can be nothing here.
en: “I don't smell anything; there can't be anything here.
ko: “저는 아무 냄새도 나지 않습니다; 여기에 그럴 만한 것이 있을 리가 없습니다.

raw: Take up the pen and finish.
en: Pick up the pen and finish writing.
ko: 펜을 들고 마저 적으십시오.

raw: Hurry, hurry!”
en: Hurry, hurry!”
ko: 서두르십시오, 서둘러요!”

raw: As if his memory were impaired, or his faculties disordered, the prisoner made an effort to rally his attention.
en: As if his mind were failing or his thoughts were confused, Darnay tried to focus.
ko: 마치 정신이 흐려지거나 생각이 뒤죽박죽된 것처럼, 다네이는 집중하려고 애를 썼다.

raw: As he looked at Carton with clouded eyes and with an altered manner of breathing, Carton--his hand again in his breast--looked steadily at him.
en: He stared at Carton with foggy eyes, his breathing changing, while Carton, keeping his hand in his coat once more, looked steadily back at him.
ko: 그는 흐릿한 눈으로 카턴을 응시하며 숨소리가 거칠어졌고, 카턴은 다시 한 번 코트 안에 손을 넣은 채 묵묵히 그를 마주 보았다.

raw: “Hurry, hurry!”
en: “Hurry, hurry!”
ko: “서두르십시오, 서둘러요!”

raw: The prisoner bent over the paper, once more.
en: Darnay bent over the paper again.
ko: 다네이는 다시 종이 위로 몸을 구부렸다.

raw: “‘If it had been otherwise;’” Carton’s hand was again watchfully and softly stealing down; “‘I never should have used the longer opportunity.
en: “‘If it had been otherwise,’” Carton's hand crept watchfully and gently down again. “‘I never would have used this longer opportunity.
ko: “‘만약 그렇지 않았다면,’” 카턴의 손이 주의 깊고 조심스럽게 다시 내려왔다. “‘저는 결코 이 길어진 기회를 사용하지 않았을 것입니다.

raw: If it had been otherwise;’” the hand was at the prisoner’s face; “‘I should but have had so much the more to answer for.
en: If it had been otherwise,’” Carton's hand was now right at Darnay's face. “‘I would only have had more to answer for.
ko: 만약 그렇지 않았다면,’” 카턴의 손은 이제 다네이의 얼굴 바로 앞에 와 있었다. “‘저는 오직 책임져야 할 것만 더 많아졌을 것입니다.

raw: If it had been otherwise--’” Carton looked at the pen and saw it was trailing off into unintelligible signs.
en: If it had been otherwise, ’” Carton looked at the pen and saw that the writing was trailing off into squiggles.
ko: 만약 그렇지 않았다면, ’” 카턴은 펜을 바라보다가 글씨가 구불구불한 낙서로 변해가는 것을 보았다.

raw: Carton’s hand moved back to his breast no more.
en: Carton did not hide his hand inside his coat again.
ko: 카턴은 더 이상 코트 안에 손을 숨기지 않았다.

raw: The prisoner sprang up with a reproachful look, but Carton’s hand was close and firm at his nostrils, and Carton’s left arm caught him round the waist.
en: Darnay jumped up with a look of surprise and blame, but Carton pressed the drugged cloth firmly over his nose and mouth, catching him around the waist with his left arm.
ko: 다네이가 놀라움과 원망이 섞인 표정으로 벌떡 일어났지만, 카턴은 그의 코와 입에 마취약이 묻은 천을 꽉 누르며 왼팔로 그의 허리를 끌어안았다.

raw: For a few seconds he faintly struggled with the man who had come to lay down his life for him; but, within a minute or so, he was stretched insensible on the ground.
en: For a few seconds, Darnay struggled weakly against the man who had come to die for him; but within a minute, he collapsed unconscious on the floor.
ko: 몇 초 동안 다네이는 자신을 대신해 죽으러 온 남자를 상대로 힘없이 발버둥쳤지만; 1분도 채 안 되어 그는 의식을 잃고 바닥에 쓰러졌다.

raw: Quickly, but with hands as true to the purpose as his heart was, Carton dressed himself in the clothes the prisoner had laid aside, combed back his hair, and tied it with the ribbon the prisoner had worn.
en: Quickly, and with hands as steady as his heart, Carton dressed himself in the clothes Darnay had taken off. He combed back his hair and tied it with Darnay's hair ribbon.
ko: 카턴은 심장만큼이나 안정된 손놀림으로 재빨리 다네이가 벗어놓은 옷을 입었다. 그는 머리를 뒤로 빗어 넘기고 다네이의 머리 리본으로 묶었다.

raw: Then, he softly called, “Enter there!
en: Then he called softly, “Come in!
ko: 그러고 나서 그가 부드럽게 불렀다, “들어오시오!

raw: Come in!” and the Spy presented himself.
en: Come in!” and Barsad the spy entered.
ko: 들어오시오!” 그러자 스파이 바사드가 들어왔다.

raw: “You see?” said Carton, looking up, as he kneeled on one knee beside the insensible figure, putting the paper in the breast: “is your hazard very great?”
en: “You see?” said Carton, looking up as he knelt beside the unconscious man, putting the letter into his coat pocket. “Is your risk very big?”
ko: “보시오?” 카턴이 의식을 잃은 남자 곁에 무릎을 꿇은 채 고개를 들어 편지를 코트 주머니에 넣으며 말했다. “당신의 위험이 매우 크오?”

raw: “Mr.
en: “Mr.
ko: “선생.

raw: Carton,” the Spy answered, with a timid snap of his fingers, “my hazard is not _that_, in the thick of business here, if you are true to the whole of your bargain.”
en: Carton,” the spy answered, snapping his fingers nervously, “my risk is not even _that_ much in all the busy rush here, as long as you keep your end of the deal.”
ko: 카턴,” 스파이가 초조하게 손가락을 튕기며 대답했다, “당신이 거래의 약속을 지키는 한, 이 바쁜 와중에 제 위험은 _그리_ 크지조차 않습니다.”

raw: “Don’t fear me.
en: “Do not fear.
ko: “두려워하지 마시오.

raw: I will be true to the death.”
en: I will keep my word to the death.”
ko: 나는 죽을 때까지 내 약속을 지킬 것이오.”

raw: “You must be, Mr.
en: “You must, Mr.
ko: “반드시 그러셔야 합니다, 선생.

raw: Carton, if the tale of fifty-two is to be right.
en: Carton, if our count of fifty-two is to be correct.
ko: 카턴, 쉰두 명이라는 우리의 계산이 맞으려면 말입니다.

raw: Being made right by you in that dress, I shall have no fear.”
en: Since you will replace him in those clothes, I have no fear.”
ko: 당신이 그 옷을 입고 그를 대신할 테니, 저는 아무런 두려움이 없습니다.”

raw: “Have no fear!
en: “Have no fear!
ko: “두려워할 것 없소!

raw: I shall soon be out of the way of harming you, and the rest will soon be far from here, please God!
en: I will soon be gone where I cannot harm you, and the others will soon be far away, God willing!
ko: 나는 곧 당신에게 해를 끼칠 수 없는 곳으로 떠날 것이고, 신이 허락하신다면 다른 이들은 곧 멀리 가 있을 것이오!

raw: Now, get assistance and take me to the coach.”
en: Now, get some help and take him to the carriage.”
ko: 자, 사람을 불러 그를 마차로 데려가시오.”

raw: “You?” said the Spy nervously.
en: “You?” the spy asked nervously.
ko: “당신을요?” 스파이가 불안한 듯 물었다.

raw: “Him, man, with whom I have exchanged.
en: “Him, man, the one I swapped places with!
ko: “그를 말이오, 이 사람아, 나와 자리를 바꾼 사람 말이지!

raw: You go out at the gate by which you brought me in?”
en: You are going out through the same gate you brought me in, aren't you?”
ko: 당신이 나를 들여보냈던 그 문으로 나갈 거 아니오?”

raw: “Of course.”
en: “Of course.”
ko: “물론이죠.”

raw: “I was weak and faint when you brought me in, and I am fainter now you take me out.
en: “I was weak and dizzy when you brought me in, and I am even weaker now that you are taking me out.
ko: “당신이 나를 데리고 들어왔을 때 나는 허약하고 어지러웠으며, 지금 나를 데리고 나가는 이 순간에는 더욱 약해져 있소.

raw: The parting interview has overpowered me.
en: The final goodbye was too much for me.
ko: 마지막 작별 인사는 내게 너무 벅찼던 거요.

raw: Such a thing has happened here, often, and too often.
en: This sort of thing has happened here many times.
ko: 이런 일은 이곳에서 여러 번 있었소.

raw: Your life is in your own hands.
en: Your life is in your own hands.
ko: 당신의 목숨은 당신 손에 달려 있소.

raw: Quick! Call assistance!”
en: Quick, call for help!”
ko: 빨리, 사람을 부르시오!”

raw: “You swear not to betray me?” said the trembling Spy, as he paused for a last moment.
en: “You swear you won't betray me?” the trembling spy asked, pausing one last time.
ko: “저를 배신하지 않겠다고 맹세하시죠?” 떨고 있던 스파이가 마지막으로 머뭇거리며 물었다.

raw: “Man, man!” returned Carton, stamping his foot; “have I sworn by no solemn vow already, to go through with this, that you waste the precious moments now?
en: “Man, man!” Carton replied, stamping his foot. “Haven't I already sworn a solemn oath to go through with this? Why are you wasting precious time?
ko: “이 사람아!” 카턴이 발을 구르며 대답했다. “내가 이미 이 일을 끝까지 해내겠다고 엄숙히 맹세하지 않았소? 왜 금쪽같은 시간을 낭비하는 거요?

raw: Take him yourself to the courtyard you know of, place him yourself in the carriage, show him yourself to Mr.
en: Take him to the courtyard yourself, put him in the carriage yourself, show him to Mr. Lorry yourself, tell Mr.
ko: 당신이 직접 그를 안뜰로 데려가서 마차에 태우고, 당신이 직접 그를 로리 씨에게 보여주고,

raw: Lorry, tell him yourself to give him no restorative but air, and to remember my words of last night, and his promise of last night, and drive away!”
en: Lorry to give him nothing but fresh air to wake him up, tell him to remember my words and promise from last night, and drive away!”
ko: 로리 씨에게 오직 신선한 공기만을 쐬게 하여 그를 깨우라고 전하고, 어젯밤에 한 나의 말과 약속을 기억하라고 전한 뒤 마차를 출발시키시오!”

raw: The Spy withdrew, and Carton seated himself at the table, resting his forehead on his hands.
en: The spy left, and Carton sat at the table, resting his head in his hands.
ko: 스파이는 떠났고, 카턴은 탁자에 앉아 두 손에 머리를 기댔다.

raw: The Spy returned immediately, with two men.
en: The spy returned immediately with two helpers.
ko: 스파이는 두 명의 조수를 데리고 즉시 돌아왔다.

raw: “How, then?” said one of them, contemplating the fallen figure. “So afflicted to find that his friend has drawn a prize in the lottery of Sainte Guillotine?”
en: “What's this?” one of them said, looking down at the unconscious man. “Is he so sad to find that his friend has won a ticket to Saint Guillotine?”
ko: “이게 뭡니까?” 그들 중 한 명이 의식을 잃은 남자를 내려다보며 말했다. “자신의 친구가 단두대로 가는 표를 얻은 것을 알고 이토록 슬퍼하는 거요?”

raw: “A good patriot,” said the other, “could hardly have been more afflicted if the Aristocrat had drawn a blank.”
en: “A good patriot,” said the other, “could hardly be sadder if the aristocrat had escaped.”
ko: “훌륭한 애국자라면,” 다른 한 명이 말했다, “귀족이 도망쳤다고 해도 이보다 더 슬퍼하진 않을 거요.”

raw: They raised the unconscious figure, placed it on a litter they had brought to the door, and bent to carry it away.
en: They lifted the unconscious Darnay, placed him on a stretcher they had brought to the door, and carried him away.
ko: 그들은 의식을 잃은 다네이를 들어 올려, 문 앞까지 가져온 들것에 눕힌 뒤 그를 데리고 나갔다.

raw: “The time is short, Evrémonde,” said the Spy, in a warning voice.
en: “Time is short, Evrémonde,” the spy said in a warning voice.
ko: “시간이 없소, 에브레몽드,” 스파이가 경고하는 목소리로 말했다.

raw: “I know it well,” answered Carton. “Be careful of my friend, I entreat you, and leave me.”
en: “I know it well,” Carton replied. “Take care of my friend, I beg you, and leave me.”
ko: “나도 잘 알고 있소,” 카턴이 대답했다. “부탁하건대 내 친구를 잘 보살펴 주시오. 그리고 나를 두고 가시오.”

raw: “Come, then, my children,” said Barsad. “Lift him, and come away!”
en: “Come on, my men,” said Barsad. “Lift him and let's go!”
ko: “자, 가자고,” 바사드가 말했다. “그를 들어 올리고 출발하자!”

raw: The door closed, and Carton was left alone.
en: The door closed, and Carton was left alone.
ko: 문이 닫혔고, 카턴은 홀로 남겨졌다.

raw: Straining his powers of listening to the utmost, he listened for any sound that might denote suspicion or alarm.
en: Listening as hard as he could, he waited for any sound of suspicion or alarm.
ko: 그는 온 신경을 곤두세운 채 의심이나 경보의 소리가 들리는지 기다렸다.

raw: There was none.
en: There was none.
ko: 아무 소리도 들리지 않았다.

raw: Keys turned, doors clashed, footsteps passed along distant passages: no cry was raised, or hurry made, that seemed unusual.
en: Keys turned, doors slammed, and footsteps echoed down distant hallways; no one shouted or rushed in a way that seemed unusual.
ko: 열쇠가 돌아가고, 문이 쾅 닫히고, 멀리 복도에서 발소리가 울려 퍼졌으나; 평소와 다르게 소리를 지르거나 서두르는 사람은 없었다.

raw: Breathing more freely in a little while, he sat down at the table, and listened again until the clock struck Two.
en: Breathing a little easier after a while, he sat down at the table and listened until the clock struck two.
ko: 잠시 후 조금 편하게 숨을 쉬며, 그는 탁자에 앉아 시계가 두 시를 칠 때까지 귀를 기울였다.

raw: Sounds that he was not afraid of, for he divined their meaning, then began to be audible.
en: Sounds that did not frighten him, because he knew what they meant, began to echo.
ko: 그가 무엇을 의미하는지 알고 있었기에 그를 두렵게 하지 않는 소리들이 울려 퍼지기 시작했다.

raw: Several doors were opened in succession, and finally his own.
en: Several cell doors were opened one after another, and finally his own.
ko: 몇 개의 감방 문이 차례로 열렸고, 마침내 그의 문이 열렸다.

raw: A gaoler, with a list in his hand, looked in, merely saying, “Follow me, Evrémonde!” and he followed into a large dark room, at a distance.
en: A jailer holding a list looked in and simply said, “Follow me, Evrémonde!” Carton followed him down to a large, dark room.
ko: 명단을 든 간수가 안을 들여다보고는 짧게 말했다, “따라와라, 에브레몽드!” 카턴은 그를 따라 넓고 어두운 방으로 내려갔다.

raw: It was a dark winter day, and what with the shadows within, and what with the shadows without, he could but dimly discern the others who were brought there to have their arms bound.
en: It was a gloomy winter day, and between the shadows inside and out, he could barely see the other prisoners who had been brought there to have their arms tied.
ko: 우울한 겨울날이었고, 안팎의 그림자 사이로 팔이 묶이도록 그곳으로 끌려온 다른 죄수들의 모습이 희미하게 보였다.

raw: Some were standing; some seated.
en: Some were standing, some were sitting.
ko: 어떤 이들은 서 있었고, 어떤 이들은 앉아 있었다.

raw: Some were lamenting, and in restless motion; but, these were few.
en: A few were crying and pacing restlessly, but they were the minority.
ko: 소수의 몇몇 사람들은 울며 쉴 새 없이 서성거렸지만, 그들은 소수에 불과했다.

raw: The great majority were silent and still, looking fixedly at the ground.
en: The great majority were silent and still, staring fixedly at the ground.
ko: 대부분의 사람들은 말없이 가만히 땅만 뚫어지게 바라보고 있었다.

raw: As he stood by the wall in a dim corner, while some of the fifty-two were brought in after him, one man stopped in passing, to embrace him, as having a knowledge of him.
en: As Carton stood against the wall in a dark corner while others of the fifty-two were brought in, one man stopped as he passed to hug him, thinking he knew him.
ko: 쉰두 명 중 다른 사람들이 들어오는 동안 카턴이 어두운 구석의 벽에 기대어 서 있을 때, 지나가던 한 남자가 그를 아는 사람으로 착각하고 멈춰 서서 그를 안으려 했다.

raw: It thrilled him with a great dread of discovery; but the man went on.
en: This filled Carton with a terrible fear of being discovered, but the man walked on.
ko: 이는 카턴에게 발각될지도 모른다는 극도의 두려움을 안겨주었으나, 그 남자는 계속 걸어갔다.

raw: A very few moments after that, a young woman, with a slight girlish form, a sweet spare face in which there was no vestige of colour, and large widely opened patient eyes, rose from the seat where he had observed her sitting, and came to speak to him.
en: A few moments later, a young woman with a slender, girlish figure, a sweet, pale face, and large, patient eyes, got up from her seat and walked over to speak to him.
ko: 잠시 후, 가냘픈 소녀 같은 체구에, 사랑스럽고 창백한 얼굴과 인내심이 엿보이는 커다란 눈을 가진 젊은 여성이 자리에서 일어나 그에게 말을 걸기 위해 다가왔다.

raw: “Citizen Evrémonde,” she said, touching him with her cold hand. “I am a poor little seamstress, who was with you in La Force.”
en: “Citizen Evrémonde,” she said, touching him with her cold hand. “I am a poor seamstress who was in La Force prison with you.”
ko: “에브레몽드 시민,” 그녀가 차가운 손으로 그를 만지며 말했다. “저는 라 포스 감옥에 당신과 함께 있었던 불쌍한 재봉사입니다.”

raw: He murmured for answer: “True.
en: He whispered in reply: “Yes.
ko: 그는 속삭이며 대답했다: “그렇소.

raw: I forget what you were accused of?”
en: I forget, what were you accused of?”
ko: 내가 깜빡 잊었소만, 당신은 어떤 혐의를 받았소?”

raw: “Plots.
en: “Plotting.
ko: “음모죄입니다.

raw: Though the just Heaven knows that I am innocent of any.
en: Though Heaven knows I am completely innocent.
ko: 비록 하늘은 제가 완전히 결백하다는 것을 알고 있지만요.

raw: Is it likely?
en: Is it likely?
ko: 그게 가능이나 한 일인가요?

raw: Who would think of plotting with a poor little weak creature like me?”
en: Who would think to plot with a poor, weak little creature like me?”
ko: 누가 저처럼 가엾고 연약하고 작은 존재와 음모를 꾸미려 하겠어요?”

raw: The forlorn smile with which she said it, so touched him, that tears started from his eyes.
en: The sad little smile she gave touched him so deeply that tears came to his eyes.
ko: 그녀가 지은 슬프고 작은 미소가 그의 마음을 너무나 깊이 울려 그의 눈에 눈물이 고였다.

raw: “I am not afraid to die, Citizen Evrémonde, but I have done nothing.
en: “I am not afraid to die, Citizen Evrémonde, but I did nothing wrong.
ko: “저는 죽는 것이 두렵지 않아요, 시민 에브레몽드, 하지만 전 잘못한 게 없어요.

raw: I am not unwilling to die, if the Republic which is to do so much good to us poor, will profit by my death; but I do not know how that can be, Citizen Evrémonde.
en: I am willing to die if it helps the Republic, which is supposed to do so much good for us poor people. But I don't see how my death can help anyone, Citizen Evrémonde.
ko: 만약 그것이 우리 가난한 사람들을 위해 많은 좋은 일을 해야 하는 공화국에 도움이 된다면 저는 기꺼이 죽을 거예요. 하지만 제 죽음이 어떻게 누구에게 도움이 될 수 있는지 모르겠어요, 시민 에브레몽드.

raw: Such a poor weak little creature!”
en: I am such a poor, weak little thing!”
ko: 저는 정말 가엾고 연약하고 작은 존재일 뿐이에요!”

raw: As the last thing on earth that his heart was to warm and soften to, it warmed and softened to this pitiable girl.
en: As the very last thing on earth to touch his heart, he felt a deep warmth and sympathy for this poor girl.
ko: 지상에서 그의 마음을 울린 마지막 일로서, 그는 이 가엾은 소녀를 향해 깊은 따뜻함과 연민을 느꼈다.

raw: “I heard you were released, Citizen Evrémonde.
en: “I heard you were set free, Citizen Evrémonde.
ko: “석방되셨다고 들었어요, 시민 에브레몽드.

raw: I hoped it was true?”
en: I hoped it was true.”
ko: 사실이길 바랐어요.”

raw: “It was.
en: “It was.
ko: “그랬지.

raw: But, I was again taken and condemned.”
en: But I was arrested again and sentenced to death.”
ko: 하지만 다시 체포되어 사형 선고를 받았습니다.”

raw: “If I may ride with you, Citizen Evrémonde, will you let me hold your hand?
en: “If I can ride in the cart with you, Citizen Evrémonde, will you let me hold your hand?
ko: “제가 시민 에브레몽드와 같은 수레를 탈 수 있다면, 제 손을 잡아주시겠어요?

raw: I am not afraid, but I am little and weak, and it will give me more courage.”
en: I am not afraid, but I am small and weak, and it will give me courage.”
ko: 두렵지는 않지만, 전 작고 연약해서 그것이 제게 용기를 줄 거예요.”

raw: As the patient eyes were lifted to his face, he saw a sudden doubt in them, and then astonishment.
en: As she raised her patient eyes to his face, he saw a sudden doubt in them, followed by shock.
ko: 그녀가 참을성 있는 눈을 들어 그의 얼굴을 바라보았을 때, 그는 그 눈에서 갑작스러운 의심과 그에 이어진 충격을 보았다.

raw: He pressed the work-worn, hunger-worn young fingers, and touched his lips.
en: He squeezed her thin, work-worn, hungry fingers and pressed them to his lips.
ko: 그는 그녀의 가늘고 일에 지쳐 굶주린 손가락을 꽉 쥐고 입술에 댔다.

raw: “Are you dying for him?” she whispered.
en: “Are you dying for him?” she whispered.
ko: “그분을 대신해 죽으시는 건가요?” 그녀가 속삭였다.

raw: “And his wife and child.
en: “And for his wife and child.
ko: “그리고 그의 아내와 아이를 위해서이기도 하오.

raw: Hush!
en: Hush!
ko: 쉿!

raw: Yes.”
en: Yes.”
ko: 그렇소.”

raw: “O you will let me hold your brave hand, stranger?”
en: “Oh, will you let me hold your brave hand, stranger?”
ko: “오, 제가 당신의 용감한 손을 잡게 해주실 건가요, 낯선 이여?”

raw: “Hush!
en: “Hush!

raw: Yes, my poor sister; to the last.” *****
en: Yes, my poor sister; all the way to the end.”
ko: 그렇소, 나의 가엾은 자매여, 끝이 날 때까지 말이오.”

raw: The same shadows that are falling on the prison, are falling, in that same hour of the early afternoon, on the Barrier with the crowd about it, when a coach going out of Paris drives up to be examined.
en: The same shadows falling on the prison were also falling, at that very hour of the early afternoon, on the city gates. A crowd stood around as a carriage leaving Paris pulled up to be checked.
ko: 이른 오후 그 시각, 감옥에 드리운 같은 그림자가 성문에도 드리우고 있었다. 파리를 떠나는 마차가 검문을 받기 위해 멈춰 서자 군중이 모여들었다.

raw: “Who goes here?
en: “Who goes there?
ko: “거기 누구냐?

raw: Whom have we within?
en: Who is inside?
ko: 안에 누가 있나?

raw: Papers!”
en: Let me see your papers!”
ko: 서류를 보여줘라!”

raw: The papers are handed out, and read.
en: The papers were handed out and read.
ko: 서류들이 건네어졌고 읽혀졌다.

raw: “Alexandre Manette.
en: “Alexandre Manette.
ko: “알렉상드르 마네트.

raw: Physician.
en: Doctor.
ko: 의사.

raw: French.
en: French.
ko: 프랑스인.

raw: Which is he?”
en: Which one is he?”
ko: 어느 사람이 그요?”

raw: This is he; this helpless, inarticulately murmuring, wandering old man pointed out.
en: This was he, the helpless, mumbling, confused old man they pointed to.
ko: 사람들이 가리키는, 무력하고 중얼거리며 혼란스러워하는 노인이 바로 그였다.

raw: “Apparently the Citizen-Doctor is not in his right mind?
en: “It seems the Citizen-Doctor is not in his right mind?
ko: “시민 의사가 제정신이 아닌 것 같군?

raw: The Revolution-fever will have been too much for him?”
en: The fever of the Revolution must have been too much for him?”
ko: 혁명의 열기가 그에게 너무 벅찼나 보지?”

raw: Greatly too much for him.
en: Much too much for him.
ko: 그에게는 너무나 벅찼다.

raw: “Hah!
en: “Hah!

raw: Many suffer with it.
en: Many people suffer from it.
ko: 많은 이들이 그런 병을 앓고 있지.

raw: Lucie.
en: Lucie.
ko: 루시.

raw: His daughter.
en: His daughter.
ko: 그의 딸.

raw: French.
en: French.
ko: 프랑스인.

raw: Which is she?”
en: Which one is she?”
ko: 어느 사람이 그 여자요?”

raw: This is she.
en: This was she.
ko: 이쪽이 그녀였다.

raw: “Apparently it must be.
en: “Clearly it is.
ko: “확실히 그렇군.

raw: Lucie, the wife of Evrémonde; is it not?”
en: Lucie, the wife of Evrémonde, correct?”
ko: 에브레몽드의 아내 루시, 맞소?”

raw: It is.
en: Yes, it is.
ko: 네, 맞습니다.

raw: “Hah!
en: “Hah!

raw: Evrémonde has an assignation elsewhere.
en: Evrémonde has an appointment elsewhere.
ko: 에브레몽드는 다른 곳에 약속이 있다.

raw: Lucie, her child.
en: Lucie, her child.
ko: 루시, 그녀의 아이.

raw: English.
en: English.
ko: 영국인.

raw: This is she?”
en: Is this she?”
ko: 이 사람이 그녀인가?”

raw: She and no other.
en: She and no other.
ko: 그녀, 바로 그 사람이다.

raw: “Kiss me, child of Evrémonde.
en: “Kiss me, child of Evrémonde.
ko: “내게 입맞춰라, 에브레몽드의 아이야.

raw: Now, thou hast kissed a good Republican; something new in thy family; remember it!
en: Now you have kissed a good Republican, something new in your family! Remember it.
ko: 이제 너는 훌륭한 공화국원에게 입을 맞춘 것이다, 네 가족에게는 새로운 일이지! 기억해 두어라.

raw: Sydney Carton.
en: Sydney Carton.
ko: 시드니 카턴.

raw: Advocate.
en: Lawyer.
ko: 변호사.

raw: English.
en: English.
ko: 영국인.

raw: Which is he?”
en: Which one is he?”
ko: 어느 쪽이 그인가?”

raw: He lies here, in this corner of the carriage.
en: He was lying in the corner of the carriage.
ko: 그는 마차 구석에 누워 있었다.

raw: He, too, is pointed out.
en: They pointed him out too.
ko: 그들은 그도 가리켰다.

raw: “Apparently the English advocate is in a swoon?”
en: “It seems the English lawyer has fainted?”
ko: “영국인 변호사가 기절한 것 같소?”

raw: It is hoped he will recover in the fresher air.
en: They hoped he would wake up in the fresh air.
ko: 그들은 그가 맑은 공기를 쐬면 깨어나길 바랐다.

raw: It is represented that he is not in strong health, and has separated sadly from a friend who is under the displeasure of the Republic.
en: They explained that he was in poor health and had just said a sad goodbye to a friend who was in trouble with the Republic.
ko: 그들은 그가 건강이 좋지 않으며, 공화국과 문제가 생긴 친구에게 방금 슬픈 작별 인사를 했다고 설명했다.

raw: “Is that all?
en: “Is that all?
ko: “그게 다요?

raw: It is not a great deal, that!
en: That's not much!
ko: 별거 아니군!

raw: Many are under the displeasure of the Republic, and must look out at the little window.
en: Many people are in trouble with the Republic, and have to look out the little window of the Guillotine.
ko: 많은 사람들이 공화국과 문제가 생겨 단두대의 작은 창밖을 내다보아야만 하니까.

raw: Jarvis Lorry.
en: Jarvis Lorry.
ko: 자비스 로리.

raw: Banker.
en: Banker.
ko: 은행가.

raw: English.
en: English.
ko: 영국인.

raw: Which is he?”
en: Which one is he?”
ko: 어느 쪽이 그인가?”

raw: “I am he.
en: “I am he.
ko: “내가 그요.

raw: Necessarily, being the last.”
en: Naturally, since I'm the last one.”
ko: 내가 마지막이니 당연하겠지.”

raw: It is Jarvis Lorry who has replied to all the previous questions.
en: Jarvis Lorry had answered all the previous questions.
ko: 자비스 로리가 이전의 모든 질문에 대답했다.

raw: It is Jarvis Lorry who has alighted and stands with his hand on the coach door, replying to a group of officials.
en: He had stepped down from the carriage and stood with his hand on the door, talking to a group of officials.
ko: 그는 마차에서 내려 문에 손을 얹고 관리들 무리와 이야기를 나누며 서 있었다.

raw: They leisurely walk round the carriage and leisurely mount the box, to look at what little luggage it carries on the roof; the country-people hanging about, press nearer to the coach doors and greedily stare in; a little child, carried by its mother, has its short arm held out for it, that it may touch the wife of an aristocrat who has gone to the Guillotine.
en: They slowly walked around the carriage and slowly climbed up to check the small amount of luggage on the roof. The local peasants standing nearby crowded closer to the carriage doors, staring greedily inside. A mother held out her little child's hand so it could touch the wife of the aristocrat who was going to the Guillotine.
ko: 그들은 마차 주변을 천천히 걷고 천천히 기어 올라가 지붕에 있는 적은 양의 수하물을 확인했다. 근처에 서 있던 지역 농민들은 마차 문으로 더 가까이 몰려들어 탐욕스럽게 안을 노려보았다. 한 어머니는 어린아이의 손을 뻗어 단두대로 갈 귀족의 아내를 만지게 했다.

raw: “Behold your papers, Jarvis Lorry, countersigned.”
en: “Here are your papers, Jarvis Lorry, stamped and signed.”
ko: “자비스 로리, 도장이 찍히고 서명된 당신의 서류들이 여기 있소.”

raw: “One can depart, citizen?”
en: “We may leave, citizen?”
ko: “우리가 떠나도 되겠소, 시민?”

raw: “One can depart.
en: “You may leave.
ko: “떠나도 좋소.

raw: Forward, my postilions!
en: Go on, drivers!
ko: 출발해라, 마부들!

raw: A good journey!”
en: Have a safe trip!”
ko: 안전한 여행 되시오!”

raw: “I salute you, citizens.--And the first danger passed!”
en: “Thank you, citizens., And the first danger is passed!”
ko: “고맙소, 시민들. 그리고 첫 번째 위험은 지나갔군!”

raw: These are again the words of Jarvis Lorry, as he clasps his hands, and looks upward.
en: These were Mr. Lorry's words as he folded his hands and looked up at the sky.
ko: 로리 씨가 두 손을 모으고 하늘을 올려다보며 한 말이었다.

raw: There is terror in the carriage, there is weeping, there is the heavy breathing of the insensible traveller.
en: There was terror and crying in the carriage, along with the heavy breathing of the unconscious traveler.
ko: 마차 안에는 의식 없는 여행자의 거친 숨소리와 함께 공포와 울음이 있었다.

raw: “Are we not going too slowly?
en: “Aren't we going too slowly?
ko: “우리 너무 천천히 가는 거 아닌가요?

raw: Can they not be induced to go faster?”  asks Lucie, clinging to the old man.
en: Can't we make them go faster?” Lucie asked, clinging to the old man.
ko: 마부들에게 더 빨리 가라고 할 수 없나요?” 루시가 노인에게 매달리며 물었다.

raw: “It would seem like flight, my darling.
en: “It would look like we are fleeing, my darling.
ko: “그러면 우리가 도망치는 것처럼 보일 거란다, 얘야.

raw: I must not urge them too much; it would rouse suspicion.”
en: I must not push them too hard; it would make them suspicious.”
ko: 내가 너무 몰아세워서는 안 돼; 그들을 의심하게 만들 거다.”

raw: “Look back, look back, and see if we are pursued!”
en: “Look back, look back, and see if anyone is chasing us!”
ko: “뒤돌아보세요, 뒤돌아보세요, 누군가 우리를 쫓아오는지 보세요!”

raw: “The road is clear, my dearest.
en: “The road is empty, my dearest.
ko: “길이 비어 있단다, 사랑하는 얘야.

raw: So far, we are not pursued.”
en: So far, no one is chasing us.”
ko: 지금까지는 아무도 우리를 쫓아오지 않는단다.”

raw: Houses in twos and threes pass by us, solitary farms, ruinous buildings, dye-works, tanneries, and the like, open country, avenues of leafless trees.
en: Houses passed by in twos and threes, along with lonely farms, ruined buildings, tanneries, open fields, and rows of leafless trees.
ko: 집들이 두세 채씩 지나갔고, 외로운 농장, 폐허가 된 건물, 무두질 공장, 탁 트인 들판, 잎이 없는 나무 줄기들이 함께 지나갔다.

raw: The hard uneven pavement is under us, the soft deep mud is on either side.
en: The carriage rode over rough, bumpy stone roads, with deep mud on both sides.
ko: 마차는 거칠고 울퉁불퉁한 돌길 위를 달렸고, 양옆으로는 깊은 진흙탕이 있었다.

raw: Sometimes, we strike into the skirting mud, to avoid the stones that clatter us and shake us; sometimes, we stick in ruts and sloughs there.
en: Sometimes we drove into the mud to avoid the stones that shook us so violently; sometimes we got stuck in ruts and puddles.
ko: 때로는 우리를 몹시 흔들리게 하는 돌들을 피하기 위해 진흙 속으로 달렸고; 때로는 바퀴 자국과 웅덩이에 갇혔다.

raw: The agony of our impatience is then so great, that in our wild alarm and hurry we are for getting out and running--hiding--doing anything but stopping.
en: The torture of waiting was so great that in our panic and hurry, we felt like jumping out of the carriage to run and hide, anything was better than sitting still.
ko: 기다림의 고문이 너무 커서 공황과 서두름 속에서 우리는 마차에서 뛰어내려 도망치고 숨고 싶었고, 가만히 앉아 있는 것보다 무엇이든 낫다고 느꼈다.

raw: Out of the open country, in again among ruinous buildings, solitary farms, dye-works, tanneries, and the like, cottages in twos and threes, avenues of leafless trees.
en: Out of the open country and back among ruined buildings, lonely farms, tanneries, cottages, and leafless trees.
ko: 탁 트인 시골을 벗어나 다시 폐허가 된 건물, 외로운 농장, 무두질 공장, 오두막, 잎이 없는 나무들 사이로 들어왔다.

raw: Have these men deceived us, and taken us back by another road?
en: Had the drivers tricked us and taken us back toward Paris?
ko: 마부들이 우리를 속이고 파리를 향해 다시 데려간 것일까?

raw: Is not this the same place twice over?
en: Was this the same place we passed before?
ko: 우리가 전에 지나갔던 곳과 같은 곳일까?

raw: Thank Heaven, no.
en: Thank goodness, no.
ko: 다행히도, 아니었다.

raw: A village.
en: It was a village.
ko: 그곳은 어느 마을이었다.

raw: Look back, look back, and see if we are pursued!
en: Look back, look back, and see if we are pursued!
ko: 뒤돌아보세요, 뒤돌아보세요, 우리가 추격당하고 있는지 보세요!

raw: Hush! the posting-house.
en: Shh, here is the carriage station.
ko: 쉿, 여기가 마차 정거장이다.

raw: Leisurely, our four horses are taken out; leisurely, the coach stands in the little street, bereft of horses, and with no likelihood upon it of ever moving again; leisurely, the new horses come into visible existence, one by one; leisurely, the new postilions follow, sucking and plaiting the lashes of their whips; leisurely, the old postilions count their money, make wrong additions, and arrive at dissatisfied results.
en: Slowly, our four horses were unhitched. Slowly, the carriage stood horse-less in the street, looking like it would never move again. Slowly, the new horses appeared one by one. Slowly, the new drivers followed, braiding the leather of their whips. Slowly, the old drivers counted their tips, did their math wrong, and grumbled about the results.
ko: 천천히, 우리의 네 마리 말이 풀렸다. 천천히, 마차는 말이 없는 채로 거리에 서서, 다시는 움직이지 않을 것처럼 보였다. 천천히, 새로운 말들이 한 마리씩 나타났다. 천천히, 새로운 마부들이 채찍의 가죽을 땋으며 뒤따랐다. 천천히, 이전 마부들은 팁을 세고, 계산을 틀리고, 그 결과에 대해 투덜거렸다.

raw: All the time, our overfraught hearts are beating at a rate that would far outstrip the fastest gallop of the fastest horses ever foaled.
en: All this time, our terrified hearts were beating at a speed that would outrun the fastest horses in the world.
ko: 그동안 우리의 겁에 질린 심장은 세상에서 가장 빠른 말들보다 더 빨리 뛰고 있었다.

raw: At length the new postilions are in their saddles, and the old are left behind.
en: At last, the new drivers were in their saddles and the old ones were left behind.
ko: 마침내, 새로운 마부들이 안장에 올랐고 이전 마부들은 뒤에 남겨졌다.

raw: We are through the village, up the hill, and down the hill, and on the low watery grounds.
en: We drove through the village, up and down a hill, and onto wet, low ground.
ko: 우리는 마을을 통과하여, 언덕을 오르내리며, 축축하고 낮은 지대로 달렸다.

raw: Suddenly, the postilions exchange speech with animated gesticulation, and the horses are pulled up, almost on their haunches.
en: Suddenly, the drivers called out to each other with wild gestures, and the horses were pulled to a sudden halt, nearly sliding on their hind legs.
ko: 갑자기 마부들이 거친 몸짓으로 서로를 부르더니, 말들이 거의 뒷다리로 미끄러지듯 갑작스럽게 멈춰 섰다.

raw: We are pursued?
en: Are we being chased?
ko: 우리가 쫓기고 있는 건가?

raw: “Ho!
en: “Hey!
ko: “이봐요!

raw: Within the carriage there.
en: Inside the carriage!
ko: 마차 안에!

raw: Speak then!”
en: Answer me!”
ko: 대답하시오!”

raw: “What is it?” asks Mr.
en: “What's wrong?” Mr.
ko: “무슨 일이오?”

raw: Lorry, looking out at window.
en: Lorry asked, looking out the window.
ko: 로리가 창밖을 내다보며 물었다.

raw: “How many did they say?”
en: “How many did they say today?”
ko: “오늘 몇 명이라고 했지?”

raw: “I do not understand you.”
en: “I don't understand you.”
ko: “무슨 말인지 모르겠소.”

raw: “--At the last post.
en: “At the last station.
ko: “마지막 정거장에서 말이오.

raw: How many to the Guillotine to-day?”
en: How many were sent to the Guillotine today?”
ko: 오늘 단두대로 보내진 사람이 몇 명이나 됩니까?”

raw: “Fifty-two.”
en: “Fifty-two.”
ko: “오십이 명이오.”

raw: “I said so!
en: “I knew it!
ko: “그럴 줄 알았지!

raw: A brave number!
en: What a great number!
ko: 대단한 숫자군!

raw: My fellow-citizen here would have it forty-two; ten more heads are worth having.
en: My friend here thought it was only forty-two; ten extra heads are always good to have.
ko: 여기 내 친구는 마흔두 명인 줄 알았지 뭡니까; 머리 열 개가 더 있으면 항상 좋지.

raw: The Guillotine goes handsomely.
en: The Guillotine is doing fine work.
ko: 단두대가 훌륭한 일을 하고 있군.

raw: I love it.
en: I love it.
ko: 정말 마음에 들어.

raw: Hi forward.
en: Move on!
ko: 출발해!

raw: Whoop!”
en: Giddy up!”
ko: 이랴!”

raw: The night comes on dark.
en: Night fell dark.
ko: 밤이 어두워졌다.

raw: He moves more; he is beginning to revive, and to speak intelligibly; he thinks they are still together; he asks him, by his name, what he has in his hand.
en: The traveler in the corner moved more; he was starting to wake up and speak clearly. He thought they were still in the cell together. He asked Carton, calling him by name, what Carton had in his hand.
ko: 구석의 여행자가 더 많이 움직였다; 그가 깨어나기 시작하며 또렷하게 말하고 있었다. 그는 그들이 아직 함께 감방에 있는 줄 알았다. 그는 카턴의 이름을 부르며, 카턴의 손에 무엇이 있는지 물었다.

raw: O pity us, kind Heaven, and help us!
en: Oh, have mercy on us, kind Heaven, and help us!
ko: 오, 자비로운 하늘이시여, 우리에게 자비를 베푸시고 우리를 도와주소서!

raw: Look out, look out, and see if we are pursued.
en: Look out, look out, and see if we are being chased.
ko: 내다보세요, 밖을 내다보세요, 그리고 우리가 쫓기고 있는지 보세요.

raw: The wind is rushing after us, and the clouds are flying after us, and the moon is plunging after us, and the whole wild night is in pursuit of us; but, so far, we are pursued by nothing else.
en: The wind rushed after us, the clouds flew above us, the moon followed us, and the whole wild night seemed to be chasing us; but, so far, nothing else was pursuing us.
ko: 바람이 우리 뒤를 몰아쳤고, 구름이 우리 위로 날아갔으며, 달이 우리를 따라왔고, 그 거친 밤 전체가 우리를 쫓고 있는 것 같았다; 하지만 아직까지는 아무것도 우리를 추격하고 있지 않았다.
